name: Image Prompt Writing Guide
description: Target-specific wording, tag vocabulary, parser syntax, negative transport, and controlled-comparison guidance for an already composed image. A section that names dialects applies only to those families. Parser, sampling and image-to-image advice requires the exact active interface to support it; model observations keep their evidenced scope.

sections.title: Model-facing language and vocabulary
rules: Render the model-facing prompt in English unless the active model record or interface provides better evidence for another language.

When a term has weak effect, first test a clearer model-legible phrase and its placement. Consider a different model only when the requested concept remains intact and the current model lacks the needed vocabulary or behavior.
Vocabulary lookup supplies options. The agent chooses, combines, rewrites, weights, or ignores them according to the request and active interface.

For a tag-oriented checkpoint with documented public training corpora, use their tag databases to check membership, canonical spelling and frequency. Frequency is weak evidence of model behavior: a rare distinctive term may work while a common term fails to express a subtle relation. Database membership does not establish behavior for another checkpoint or a prose interface.

Check candidate tags against the documented public corpora used by the selected checkpoint. Corpora can disagree about aliases and membership, so one database's absence does not settle the others. Do not infer undisclosed training corpora or require tag-database membership for a natural-language rendition.

When a tag underperforms and its documented corpus publishes a canonical alias, compare the two spellings on the selected checkpoint before abandoning it. Record the observed result rather than assuming both spellings work across models.

In a tag-oriented rendition, word adjacency alone does not establish per-subject role control. Inspect whether each figure keeps its assigned identity and role. If the active setup fails that check, consider staging, separate generations or regional conditioning supported by the selected interface.

A vocabulary resource legitimately mixes two registers: canonical tags the corpora carry, and descriptive phrasing the text encoder understands as language. Absence from a tag database is not evidence that a descriptive phrase is broken, so do not prune vocabulary on that basis alone.

Use multiple tag dialects only when the active checkpoint has evidence for them. Compare count-plus-anthro, male-plus-furry and kemono forms for subject correctness and styling separately. An observed shift toward rounder, flatter faces is specific to the tested checkpoint and settings; it does not establish interchangeability across models.

Treat a checkpoint version change as a target change. Sibling releases may differ at the same seed in default build mass, negative adherence, and prop or scenery conventions. Reassess the exact version and record the target change instead of assuming identical family behavior.

Preserve explicit parameter choices and validate them against the selected interface. Use the active record's recommendations as evidence-scoped starting points for unresolved choices, before a matching dialect baseline.

The preparation checker inspects the exact final positive and negative channels after model recommendations and transport selection. Grammar, declared limits and channel violations block preparation; complete dictionary and dialect evidence remains available for the existing author rendition review.

Vocabulary membership does not establish intended meaning. Read definitions for ambiguous anatomy or garment words. Assess an unlisted close-up phrase or speech verb from its meaning and target evidence rather than treating absence as proof of failure.

Check whether a requested local color or close-up actually remains local in the candidate. Keep target-specific spillover observations in the active model record, rather than turning one campaign into a universal vocabulary prohibition.

sections.title: Tag prompt construction
rules: For these tag-oriented dialects, use concise terms separated by a comma followed by one space, except inside a supported compound conditioning expression whose parser owns its grouping.

Render the already composed image in the active family's supported block order. Protect the terms carrying the whole scene and its relationships before adding local detail or an optional quality block. An evidenced target order may place its quality block first; that syntax choice must preserve all required content.
Do not copy a generic quality stack when the active model record provides a reviewed positive recommendation. Preserve the requested image concept rather than replacing it with boilerplate.

On a position-sensitive encoder, protect load-bearing anchors from truncation and dilution. Keep them in the effective window the exact workflow supports, remove redundant restatement, and inspect later scene blocks instead of assuming every encoder gives the first chunk the same advantage.

Before delivery, re-read each compact tag for a second model-legible sense. A region word can name gear, such as muzzle reading as a restraint device instead of the snout, and a directional body word can name a camera view, such as back pulling the render to a rear view. When a surface form collides with another sense, choose vocabulary that carries only the intended sense, such as coat-structure terms like countershading for body color zones.

A quality block consumes the same prompt capacity as scene content. Some tag checkpoints associate quality-tagged examples with simple-background character shots, so a starved environment may improve without that block. Treat it as an optional target-specific comparison and preserve content-critical terms when capacity is tight.

On a checkpoint with a strong character-focus prior, heavy build or physique tags can compete with environment instructions and favor a plain background. Verify both the required physique and setting in the result, and compare environment placement without removing identity anchors.

Region-color or region-detail tags can encourage a checkpoint to reveal that region or weaken its covering. Likewise, a garment, prop or effect tag can pull its subject into frame. Select tags for the intended depiction, retaining hidden anchors when they prevent a wrong visible inference; assess any visibility spillover in the actual result.

When a tested checkpoint loses an unusual color, bind it to each relevant region separately, such as body, arms, hands, tail or ears. For a two-tone front, compare a coat-structure term plus the small feature's color. A different covering, such as scales, needs vocabulary and observations for that material rather than a presumed noun substitution.

When the active encoder window is over capacity, trim implied and redundant tags before sacrificing required blocks. Body-build and other identity anchors retain their full specificity; select a supported method that can carry them if the target limit is insufficient.

A strongly represented content cluster can bring its own color, texture, setting and prop conventions. If that drift appears on the selected checkpoint, compare earlier identity and environment anchors and scoped negatives. Even a bare-torso subject without adult vocabulary may trigger such associations; the observation remains specific to that target and setup.

sections.title: Tag prompt grammar
rules: On a checkpoint trained on booru tags, write tags in lowercase unless the tag itself carries capitals. How a tag of more than one word is spelled is the family's own convention, which the prompt-dialects resource states per family: read it rather than assuming one form.

Separate intended tags with commas in a tag rendition. For example, sleeveless, striped shirt, collared shirt makes the chosen tag units explicit. Whether an unseparated descriptive phrase also works depends on the exact text encoder.

Escape literal syntax delimiters for the explicitly selected parser. In Compel, parentheses group a phrase and suffixes apply weights; in sdEmbeds, parentheses, square brackets and a trailing colon weight have different meanings. A learned tag family does not select the service parser.

Within one conditioning clause, prefer one explicit weight to repeated tags. Repetition across independent Compel clauses has a different scope; do not flatten clauses or silently deduplicate the author's combined expression.

On a checkpoint where detailed modifiers have a measured effect, compare detailed eyes, detailed fluffy fur or detailed background only for the elements that need that attention. Repeating the modifier everywhere does not establish a useful priority.

Weighted syntax is an interface parser feature, not inferred from a model family. Select the native promptWeighting control only when the chosen offering and execution mode expose it; otherwise treat punctuation literally rather than assuming a backend parser.

Take block order from the active family. For a supported multi-figure tag workflow, keep interaction terms with the count block and give each figure its own identity and pose scope. Separate chunks may restate the relevant count, but chunking itself does not assign spatial regions or guarantee identity separation.

Take rating and period terms from the active dialect and select a consistent intended register. A single term from each set is a useful baseline; the author evaluates a deliberate combination within its clause scope. Do not assume another family learned the same tokens.

The dialect identifies vocabulary with limited or unsupported effect on that family. Consult its corpus and model evidence before selecting those terms. Missing membership alone cannot establish that a descriptive phrase has no useful meaning.

sections.title: The Illustrious and NoobAI dialect
rules: Illustrious is trained on Danbooru tags alone. The e621 dialect (muscular_anthro, the e621 body-build and species terms) acts only on NoobAI-family checkpoints that add that corpus.
Rating tags act on Illustrious and NoobAI checkpoints: general, sensitive, questionable, and explicit steer the register of the whole image. Use one per prompt, in the quality block.

The rating general was introduced in 2022 and matches a thin slice of the corpus. For an all-ages image it is usually better left out than forced; sensitive, questionable, and explicit carry their full weight.

Period tags act on Illustrious and NoobAI checkpoints: newest, recent, mid, early, and old bias the render toward the drawing conventions of a slice of the training corpus by upload year (NoobAI documents them as 2021 to 2024, 2018 to 2020, 2014 to 2017, 2011 to 2014, and 2005 to 2010). newest is the usual choice for a current look, old is a deliberate retro finish, and the other period words in a negative push the render away from those slices. Because old is a period term here, write an elderly figure's tag whole, as old_man or old_woman.
Score-band tags such as score_9 belong to Pony-family checkpoints and are literal noise on Illustrious and NoobAI. Use the family's own quality block instead.

On these tag-trained checkpoints, 4k, 8k, hdr, high quality and detailed on its own are not established quality controls. A rare tag with fewer than about 100 corpus posts is weak evidence of a learned tag effect, not proof of incapability. A character with several historical designs may follow its dominant corpus design; verify the requested construction on the exact checkpoint.

Resolution marks describe the corpus post's pixel size, not render quality: highres is 1600x1200 and up, absurdres 3200x2400 and up, incredibly absurdres above 10000 pixels. Their only pull is toward large finished uploads, so use at most one, or none.

The family's documented order is count, character name, rating, general tags, artist, quality, period. Use the exact model's evidenced order when it differs, and hold that order fixed during a controlled comparison so a placement change is not confused with a content change.

For these checkpoints, an artist with about 100 or more corpus posts is a stronger candidate for a learned artist-tag effect than a rare one. In a compatible sdEmbeds-style parser, a reduced value such as (artist:0.5) or (traditional media:0.5) is a trial of influence, not a guaranteed partial style. Use the selected parser's own syntax and inspect the result.

sections.title: The Anima dialect
rules: Anima pairs a Qwen-series text encoder and VAE with a Danbooru tag vocabulary, so the tag register is the booru one while the sampling behaviour is not the SDXL lineage's. Use the Qwen VAE the family names; another VAE shifts colour and detail.

Anima carries both registers at once: the booru quality terms and the Pony score bands act together, and the working block is masterpiece, best quality, score_9, score_8, score_7, very aesthetic, highres, absurdres, newest. Both corpus size marks are used here rather than at most one.
Write a multi-word tag with spaces on Anima, not underscores. The score terms keep their underscores.
An artist tag needs an at sign in front of it on Anima. Without it the tag does not bind.

An explicit weight wants a higher value on Anima than on the SDXL lineage, about 1.2 to 1.4. Raise only the tags that carry the request; a high weight on everything flattens the difference it was meant to make.
Anima takes a year term beside the period term, written as year 2025 or year 2024, which narrows the period further than newest alone.
Anima's rating terms are safe, sensitive, nsfw, and explicit. The Danbooru set that the Illustrious family uses does not apply here.

Anima's block order ends with a plain-language line for what the tags cannot carry. Use it for a relation or a staging the tag vocabulary has no term for, and keep the tags carrying everything they can.

sections.title: Sampling baseline for the Illustrious and NoobAI dialect
rules: Start from Euler a. The DPM++ family tends to leave residual noise on these checkpoints at ordinary step counts.
Keep guidance between 3 and 5, with 4.5 as the working point; above 6 the colors saturate and the prompt becomes hard to steer. A distilled or LCM variant wants 4 to 8, with 6 as the working point.
About 20 steps is the working point. Raise it only when a LoRA's own page asks for it.

Generate at a trained bucket: 1024x1024, 1024x1536, 832x1216, or 768x1344. Reach a larger delivery size with a second pass, either hires fix at 1.5x with denoise 0.4 to 0.5 over a plain nearest-exact resample of the first pass (about 16 hires steps in a ComfyUI-style graph, about 40 in a Diffusers pipeline), or an upscaler pass on the accepted image. A hires factor of 2 and above breaks composition on these checkpoints.

SDXL-lineage sizes: keep about one megapixel with both sides multiples of 8, and prefer the trained buckets, which are multiples of 64: 1024x1024, 896x1152, 1152x896, 832x1216, 1216x832, 768x1344, 1344x768, 640x1536, 1536x640. For another ratio, width is 1024 times the square root of the ratio and height is 1048576 divided by the width, both rounded down to a multiple of 8 (2:3 gives 832x1248, 16:9 gives 1360x768).
A v-prediction checkpoint needs a pipeline that supports v-prediction; Automatic1111 does not, so run the eps variant there.

sections.title: Sampling baseline for the Anima dialect
rules: Start from Euler a, with er_sde as the other choice the family names, and the normal scheduler.
About 30 steps is the working point, and guidance between 4 and 6 with 5 as the working point.
Generate around 1280 pixels square, which is the size this family was trained at, and take another ratio at that same pixel count rather than at the SDXL lineage's one megapixel.

sections.title: Subject count and scene situation
rules: For a tag-oriented model, state an evidenced subject count only after reading the actual request. If exactly one depicted subject is requested, use the active dialect's supported single-subject count tag when helpful. If a group, scene without characters, or deliberately unknown count is requested, do not invent solo, 1boy, 1girl or another subject. Count tags are not universal controls for natural-language editing interfaces.

Name the environment, light and props when the requested image or authorized edit needs them; for an existing-image edit, preserve source environment when outside the change scope. Do not invent a setting or props for an unspecified background, isolated asset, or transparent cut-out. Only tag-oriented dialects use their supported location and time tags.

Render the selected scene situation through the target's supported tags. Keep background and props consistent with framing, while retaining any off-frame fact needed to explain a visible result or preserve continuity.

Multi-subject tag prompts can transfer species, color or identity between figures. If the selected setup shows that failure, compare clearer subject scopes, supported regional conditioning, or separately generated assets and compositing. Choose another production stage only when its capability and the authorized task justify it.

If multi-tag pressure causes observed species drift, especially in a side view, reinforce the approved species geometry with supported wording and, where useful, an explicit weight or color terms. A rival-species negative is a scoped correction only when it preserves the requested construction.

Carry the anthropomorphic construction needed for the current frame at full specificity. Foot posture, pads, tufts and other distinct structures may need separate terms on these checkpoints; a species tag alone does not prove their reconstruction.

sections.title: Framing and crop control
rules: Express the selected framing with supported tags. A tall portrait canvas can bias a single-character checkpoint toward full body, so compare an explicit close-crop term when that is the intended shot. A full-body request likewise needs its head-to-feet coverage preserved.

To request a tighter crop on a tag-oriented image model, use supported framing and crop tags as the active grammar allows. Add negative exclusions only if the target has a compatible negative channel and they do not conflict with the intended frame. For source-image edits, do not reframe without specific authorization.

If a blank-background crop dissolves the body instead of cutting it at the frame edge, compare a supported hard crop-state tag. A visible support surface, floor shadow or contacted prop can also clarify the edge when it belongs to the chosen scene; do not add one merely as universal crop boilerplate.

Match canvas geometry to the selected framing within the interface's accepted sizes. Squarer or landscape canvases are candidates for face or upper-body crops, and tall portrait canvases for full body; the subject and scene decide. For an explicit full body, a supported weight such as sdEmbeds (full body:1.2) is a trial, not a default. Retain needed identity detail and avoid crop-state terms that contradict the chosen coverage.
State the requested framing in the delivered plan or provenance so the choice, and any weight used to enforce it, stays visible and reversible in later edits.

When facing is required, choose the target's supported wording, such as facing viewer, front view, from behind or looking back. When it is open creative space, do not manufacture a facing constraint solely because a tag exists.

For a position-sensitive tag checkpoint, compare a leading framing term when moving from close-up to establishing shot. At part magnification, preserve that region's full identity anchors; framing vocabulary alone does not carry its construction.

A plain-background tag can also tighten the crop on a checkpoint whose plain-background and close-character examples overlap. Review its effect on the selected framing rather than assuming background and camera controls are independent.

When scene bias defeats a plain-background tag in a standing-figure asset, compare the supported sheet, background, view, full-body and standing terms, weighting only the needed terms with the selected parser. Another authorized method is an accepted scene render followed by background removal. These alternatives can change finish and layout, so evaluate them against the intended asset.

Some tag checkpoints do not resolve a requested orthographic top or bottom view from a camera tag alone. A from-above comparison may remain near fifty degrees and from-below near thirty; bird's-eye or worm's-eye wording can also be read literally. Treat these as possible failure patterns to inspect, not universal angle limits. Use suitable spatial guidance when the required view remains unresolved.

A sheet tag can introduce panels, pseudo-text and swatches on these checkpoints. Omit it when those elements are unwanted and the existing layout stage owns the sheet; retain it when the image itself requires the supported sheet construction.

sections.title: Expression and performance
rules: Choose expression and visible body-language cues when the brief, character identity or scene state calls for them. For an edit, retain the source expression unless the task changes it; do not insert a new expression or appendage state as a universal default.

For these tag dialects, compare a small coordinated cluster of eye, mouth and posture cues when one expression tag fails to carry the selected performance. Use applicable production knowledge without expanding the performance beyond its intended scope.

On a position-sensitive setup, protect the performance block alongside composition-critical tags rather than leaving it after a long attribute inventory. Inspect the actual acting when comparing placement.

When the exact target supports short relational phrases, name who does what to whom and inspect both subjects. A conventional action term can carry its own camera or staging prior; compare supported position terms and descriptive geometry within the chosen setup instead of assuming either form always wins.

sections.title: Prompt budget and visible scope
rules: Determine capacity, chunking and truncation from the active encoder and workflow. Some Automatic1111-style CLIP workflows chunk beyond a 75-token window; other CLIP paths can truncate without chunking support. ComfyUI, Diffusers and web forms host different models and pipelines, so their names alone establish no universal token ceiling.
Do not spend limited prompt budget on off-frame details unless they are continuity anchors, reference-authority constraints, or needed to prevent a wrong visible inference.

When an off-frame garment or body-detail tag degrades visible anatomy and is not load-bearing for the current frame, omit it from the model-facing rendition while retaining it in the underlying identity or scene state.

sections.title: Chunking and regional passes for supported tag workflows
rules: Use BREAK only when the exact parser supports it. A separately encoded environment block can resist attention loss in an earlier block, but chunking does not guarantee full visual influence. Review count and identity across chunks and restate needed scope where the target requires it.

When a target cannot carry the complete scene in one supported input, consider authorized regional passes: establish the base image, then scope an inpaint prompt to the changed region and its required eye color, expression or garment. Preserve the rest through the actual supplied source and the interface's edit controls.

sections.title: Attention weighting
rules: Use attention syntax only when the active parser supports the demonstrated grammar. Parentheses and square brackets are not portable across all image interfaces.
Use weighting sparingly to express a genuine priority. Do not use extreme weights to compensate for contradictory anatomy, camera, action, or reference authority.
Nested emphasis compounds when the parser applies the same multiplier at each level. Explicit numeric weights state the requested multiplier directly.

In sdEmbeds-style syntax, a colon and numeric weight bind at the end of a parenthesized fragment: (term:1.2). Compel instead uses (term)1.2, term+ or (multiple words)--. Keep the grammar consistent with the selected native control; CPB does not translate the author's expression between them.

Malformed, misplaced or mixed weighting syntax can be interpreted as unintended literal text by a backend. Inspect the complete final positive and negative rendition using the selected parser and correct mechanical findings before authorizing a request.

Emphasis grammars are interface-bound. Curly-brace emphasis is not Compel or sdEmbeds weighting. When changing parser, author a new reviewed rendition and request; do not let software silently convert bracket shapes or coefficients.

Compel .blend() combines conditioning and .and() combines separately encoded chunks. They are not spatial region assignments or a guarantee that characters retain separate roles. An uppercase AND or BREAK is not the same operator; only use syntax documented for the chosen interface.

Down-weighting the only tag carrying an attribute can let a checkpoint return to its default rather than produce an intermediate state. For example, reducing a sole environment anchor need not dim the scene. Compare an explicit intermediate description at ordinary weight on the selected target.

In a compatible sdEmbeds-style parser, square-bracket reduction may be too weak against a strong checkpoint prior, while nested emphasis can also alter related content or late garment tags. Prefer explicit numeric comparisons and inspect the entire result; these are possible effects, not guaranteed semantic multipliers.

examples.effect: Approximately 1.1x emphasis in parsers that implement Automatic1111-style attention syntax.
Approximately 1.21x emphasis when two nested pairs each apply about 1.1x.
Approximately 1/1.1x emphasis, about 0.91x, in compatible parsers.
Explicit 0.25x attention, or one quarter of the unweighted level, in compatible parsers.

In the declared sdEmbeds-style grammar, this does not bind 0.9 to term as an explicit terminal weight. The number remains inside the fragment. Correct the grammar; the resulting image effect cannot be inferred from those literal digits.
About 1.05x emphasis in NovelAI's native parser only. Automatic1111-style parsers do not read braces as emphasis.
Compel: an explicit group coefficient and a suffix on the final word. Not sdEmbeds colon syntax.
Compel: independent conditioning chunks; not a regional assignment. Review the combined intent.
Compel: weighted conditioning blend. Clause coefficients are retained; the provider computes embeddings.

sections.title: LoRA strength
rules: Use the active model or LoRA record's reviewed strength recommendation when one exists.

On a compatible SDXL-style LoRA strength scale, 0.7 to 0.8 can be a declared trial starting point when no better record exists. Other scales require their own evidence. Tune against under-activation, overbaking, identity drift and unwanted finish changes.
When comparing strengths, change one LoRA weight at a time and keep the remaining generation conditions constant.

sections.title: Wardrobe trials in supported tag image-to-image workflows
rules: An image-to-image source can retain garments despite a requested wardrobe change. A strength near or below 0.7 is a possible trial condition on compatible denoise scales, not a universal preservation threshold. Determine whether garment wording and source influence conflict with the intended change; a state tag alone may invent an unspecified garment.

When a permitted wardrobe change fails on the selected checkpoint, compare garment terms earlier in the prompt, supported garment emphasis, a guidance adjustment, or an accepted source of the same character at a suitable image-to-image strength. A combined repair changes several factors and cannot identify one cause. Inspect color drift, stray marks and identity changes associated with garment vocabulary.

sections.title: Negative prompts and embeddings
rules: The active adapter and model record own negative transport. Use a separate negative field only when the interface exposes and supports it; otherwise follow the adapter's integrated or native-subset contract.

Use the negative-policy resource to assess source applicability. The active dialect's negative_form supplies wording candidates for a supported negative channel; the author preserves the intended scope of every selected exclusion.

A Textual Inversion embedding is a selected model resource, not a universal replacement for a reviewed negative prompt. Use its exact activation token and weight only when the active workflow supports it.
Do not infer that a model family needs no negative handling merely from its name. Follow the exact active workflow record.

sections.title: Negative blocks for the selected tag dialect
rules: Review any reused negative block as four separable strata before adoption: the active family's reviewed quality terms, deliberately weighted content gates, corrections scoped to an observed failure, and residue carried from other model families or abandoned workflows. Keep the first three intentional and drop the residue.

Use family-bound rating or score-band tokens only where the exact checkpoint supports them. A Textual Inversion token requires its selected embedding to be loaded; otherwise it provides no evidenced embedding control.

Read the positive and negative clauses together. A negative naming the desired subject or an essential attribute may conflict, or it may address another region or subject. Resolve the actual meaning and scope instead of deleting a lexical overlap automatically.

Inspect duplicate terms inside each negative conditioning clause. Preserve distinct .blend()/.and() clauses and their weights; terms repeated across clauses are not mechanically flattened into a single negative list.

For a position-sensitive negative encoder, place the scene's important exclusions where the workflow preserves them. Compare their effect before carrying a reusable defect block that consumes the same capacity.

Keep all necessary exclusions and remove redundant or irrelevant terms. There is no universal negative-term count that establishes instability or permits dropping required constraints. Check the exact encoder's limits and the observed result.

A weighted negative may fail to suppress content explicitly requested by a positive clause. Resolve a real contradiction at its source. For observed unintended drift, such as a color reverting to the checkpoint default, compare a scoped exclusion without weakening the wanted attribute.

Exclude the observed drift at its actual scope. A neighboring-color negative can also shift the wanted color; for example, an orange exclusion may disturb amber eyes. Inspect the selected checkpoint's result rather than assuming independent color controls.

For a family with rating tokens, choose the intended register using its evidenced vocabulary. A negative content gate can address unintended drift but does not guarantee that conflicting positive content will be suppressed.

sections.title: Controlled term comparison
rules: When evaluating one term, hold the checkpoint or model, LoRA set and weights, seed, sampler, scheduler, steps, guidance value, dimensions, base prompt, negative transport, and references constant. Keep the native promptWeighting parser selection constant too; a grammar switch is a separate experimental change.
Change one term, one weight, or one placement at a time so the observed difference has a clear cause.
When placement sensitivity is under review, compare the same term near the beginning and near the end without changing any other condition.
A controlled comparison measures one active setup. Do not promote a single result into a universal model rule.
Treat sampler, scheduler, steps, guidance, dimensions, seed, model hash, and similar values in a prompt example as reproducibility metadata for that example, not as universal defaults.

sections.title: Compatible WebUI editing shortcut
rules: In editors that implement the Automatic1111-style shortcut, select a term and use Ctrl+Up or Ctrl+Down to change its explicit attention weight by 0.1.
This is an editor convenience, not portable model-facing syntax. Do not describe it as available unless the active interface supports it.

sections.title: Select service weighting separately from learned vocabulary
rules: Resolve the exact native promptWeighting control for the model, service and execution mode. A service-wide explanation mentioning Compel and sdEmbeds is not evidence every model accepts both.

Compel + is 1.1 per suffix and - is 0.9 per suffix; an unweighted parenthesized group has no implicit boost. Do not substitute sdEmbeds brackets or multiply their defaults as though the embeddings were equivalent.
The final prepared request is the source of syntax selection. Review parsed positive and negative clauses, original text, dictionary notes and model recommendations together before approval.

For compound conditioning expressions, keep automatic recommendations as visible advice until the author places them in the intended clauses. Never prepend a global fragment that breaks expression scope.
CPB inspects syntax with the standard library; the provider runs conditioning. No local Compel, PyTorch, Transformers or browser installation is part of this feature.
